lead_headline: Restaurant tracker goes dark — zero new leads detected Tuesday despite 287-lead pipeline still active

restaurant.blurb: Zero new leads today. Active pipeline holds at 287 (156 openings, 131 closures). Tracker quiet for second straight day.

liquor.blurb: Single new application today: The Runway and Rye Lounge filing for hotel/restaurant license at DIA (8900 Pena Blvd). Plus 5 status changes — three neighborhood liquor stores (Patio, Federal Theatre, Viejo) flipped delinquent, while Target T3403 on Quebec and Bamboo Sushi on Madison both resolved to active. Week's total now 334 applications following Monday's 333-app deluge that broke the state's 45-day freeze. Pipeline activity remains elevated after six-week blackout — 7-day window showing genuine licensing movement for first time since late May.

reputation.blurb: 2 citations yesterday — Tuesday matching Monday's anemic pace after the weekend lull. Week crawls to 80 mentions across 17 sources, still tracking 7% above last week's 75 but momentum clearly stalling. Instagram retains the lead at 19 (unchanged from Monday), Denver Post at 17, Facebook 14. Notable pickups: gasthof-zur-schwane.de running 137-year-old church conversion story, Instagram post on serial eviction case gaining traction. The three-week uptrend (72 → 75 → 80) flattens as daily acquisition drops to 2-3 citations — well below the 10-11/day pace needed to sustain growth. Source diversity contracts to 17 outlets from Monday's 18. Five days remain to salvage July's weekly average.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (0 new, 1 canceled) — twelfth consecutive day underwater. MTD sinks deeper to −5 (−0.4/day), while 90-day cumulative holds at +104. The July bloodletting continues: twelve straight negative days now erase any monthly momentum, with acquisition completely frozen at zero for two consecutive sessions. Since July 1, just 17 new subscribers against 35 cancellations — a catastrophic −18 net that accelerates into the worst fortnight on record. Past 7 days show −14 net (17 new, 31 canceled) vs. prior week's +9 — a 23-subscriber swing that confirms the churn crisis deepening. Cancellation rate now running 1.8:1 against new sign-ups. If the pattern persists through month-end, July will mark the first negative monthly net in tracking history. Zero recovery signal visible entering mid-month.
